notes: 1. JBP = Joint Business Plan. A CP submits ONE plan per OPEN JBP cycle declaring sales/booking targets, marketing-investment commitments and resource plans (manpower, activities, digital channels). One active submission per CP per cycle (BRD §4.5, FS 1.2/1.5 Rule 2).

2. CP portal entry: Mobile-OTP only (no password). UAT mobile = 8888888888, CP static OTP = 147258 (NOT 258369 — that is the Admin/SM OTP). Successful login lands on /dashboard; JBP is reached via the 'JBP' sidebar item.

3. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] = a disposable UAT record/state must be supplied before executing this test. EVERY test that SUBMITS/CREATES a JBP, files an EDIT REQUEST, or otherwise WRITES a live record is marked [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] and also carries a mutation-authorisation note — JBP submission WRITES live records (JbpSubmission row, LSQ activity, Botspice WhatsApp). DO NOT click Submit / file an edit request on the live UAT CP fixture without explicit user authorisation (CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline rule 7).
4. [VERIFY WITH DEV] = behaviour not confirmed in BRD/FRD/FS or not transcribed in visual-memory; confirm before treating Pass/Fail as authoritative.

5. JBP cycle states: a cycle is OPEN or CLOSED. The CP can submit only while OPEN (BRD §4.6, FS 1.5 Rule 1). When CLOSED the form is unavailable and a 'Cycle has Closed' message is shown (visual-memory screenshot-desktop.png baseline, 2026-06-03). 'Your Status' pill values: Not Submitted | Submitted | Approved | Rejected.

6. CYCLE-DEPENDENT EVIDENCE: visual-memory was captured against the OPEN cycle 'Automation JBP / June 2026 / Closes 30th June 2026'. The CLOSED-cycle UI was captured earlier against 'test JBP / May 2026'. Cycle names/dates in steps are illustrative of whatever cycle is OPEN at execution time — read the live Current Cycle card, do not hard-assert 'Automation JBP'.

7. POST-SUBMIT EDIT FLOW: After submitting, the CP cannot self-edit. Changes go via an admin-reviewed edit request (Edit Requests tab). Approved → submission updated, version increments (v1→v2), old version marked EXPIRED (BRD §4.7, FS 2.4). Rejected → original preserved, CP receives the reason. Admin-side approval/rejection is performed in the Admin Portal > JBP Management > Submissions/Edit-Requests — out of scope for the CP portal screen but verified end-to-end where flagged XMOD/E2E.

8. SILENT-UX RULE: a missing toast/confirmation is NOT a bug if the backend side-effect occurred. Verify the JbpSubmission row / redirect to /jbp/thank-you / version change before flagging a defect (CLAUDE.md Pipeline Discipline rule 6, feedback_silent_ux_not_bug.md).

9. GLOSSARY of on-screen labels (from visual-memory): page heading 'JBP Dashboard'; sub-heading 'Current Cycle - <cycleName>'; tabs 'Current Cycle Entry' (default) / 'JBP History' / 'Edit Requests'; empty-state text 'No submission for current cycle' + primary CTA 'Add New JBP Entry'; form heading 'JBP Form - <cycleName>'; brokerage field placeholder 'Select Brokerage'; registration-commitment field placeholder 'Enter Count'; form-footer buttons 'Back to Dashboard' and 'Submit'.

10. DOC_DRIFT-001 (URL) — BRD (CP-BRD-CP-Portal.md / CP-FRD-CP-Portal.md) and FS (CP-FS-JBP-Submission.md) state the JBP URL as https://uat.xrportal.in/jbp. visual-memory INDEX.md + both DOM sidecars show the live route is https://uat-web.xrportal.in/jbp. Live implementation wins (uat-web.xrportal.in/jbp); TCs use the observed host. BRD/FRD/FS URL should be corrected to uat-web.xrportal.in.

11. DOC_DRIFT-002 (form layout) — FS 1.4 documents 14 logical fields with friendly labels (Brokerage, Net Booking Commitment, Manpower+Slider, List of Activities (14), Go Live on Digital, Total Investment (5 radio ranges), 7 Yes/No fields, Registration Commitment). visual-memory INDEX.md summarises the rendered DOM as 44 inputs: 1 Brokerage ant-select, 1 untyped text, 20 checkboxes, '9 radio-groups of 2 each (18 radios)', 1 'Enter Count' text. The actual sidecar _jbp-form-inspect.json shows EIGHT radio-groups / 19 radios: group ':rt:' has FIVE options (= Total Investment 5 ranges) and seven groups (':ru:' ':rv:' ':r10:' ':r11:' ':r12:' ':r13:' ':r14:') have two options each (= the 7 Yes/No fields: Inserts, Standees, Kiosk, Tele Callers, SMS Blast, WhatsApp Blast, Growth Hub). So the INDEX.md '9 groups × 2 = 18' summary is itself slightly inaccurate vs its own sidecar. Field human-labels did not surface in the DOM dump (no aria-label / non-sibling <label>). TCs reference the FS friendly labels for intent and the screenshot for placement; exact on-screen label strings beside each control are [VERIFY WITH DEV] against the live render.

12. DOC_DRIFT-003 (activity count) — FS 1.4 says 'List of Activities (14 options)'. Existing TC CP_JBP_009 records the live UI shows 15 activity options ('15 options (not 14)'). The 20-checkbox grid is Activities + 'Go Live on Digital' channels combined. Treat 15 activities as the observed count; FS '14' is stale.

13. SECURITY / KNOWN-BUG notes carried from prior pass (existing TCs): CP_JBP_036 project-ownership NOT enforced (BUG); CP_JBP_029 non-existent jbpCycleId causes a backend NPE (BUG); CP_JBP_040 isJbpSubmitted login flag counts EXPIRED rows (BUG). These remain documented, not silently dropped. New security/auth cases added below ([VERIFY WITH DEV] where backend behaviour is unconfirmed).

14. NOTIFICATIONS: a successful JBP submission triggers a Botspice WhatsApp template 'jbplaunchtwo_new' (15 vars) per CP_JBP_035 — NOT Kaleyra. The edit-request REJECTION path sends no push notification per CP_JBP_027. OTP SMS for CP login is via Epinet. LSQ createActivity/captureLead are called on submit (CP_JBP_033/034).

tcs.precond: The JBP form is open with required non-checkbox fields filled. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] authorised disposable submission to reach Submit.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill all required fields but tick no checkboxes.
2. Click 'Submit'.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] FS does not state whether at least one Activity/Digital channel is required. [To verify] confirm whether zero-checkbox submission is accepted or blocked.

tcs.scenario: To verify the form fields accept user input via UI interactions
tcs.description: Verify that all field types (select, checkboxes, radios, count) accept genuine click/keyboard input.
tcs.precond: The JBP form is open.
tcs.steps:
1. Select a Brokerage option.
2. Tick several Activities and Digital checkboxes.
3. Choose a Total Investment range.
4. Set each Yes/No field.
5. Type a value in 'Enter Count'.
tcs.testData: Representative valid values across all fields
tcs.expected: Every control reflects the entered value (selected option, ticked boxes, chosen radios, typed count); the form is fully populated and ready to submit. (Note: prior JS-injection fill only populated ~2 inputs; real fill is click-driven — visual-memory Form Filled Behaviour.)

tcs.scenario: To verify a successful JBP submission
tcs.description: Verify that submitting a complete, valid JBP creates the submission and shows the Thank You confirmation.
tcs.precond: An OPEN cycle exists; the CP has not yet submitted; all required fields are filled. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a disposable CP with an open cycle. MUTATION: writes a live JbpSubmission + LSQ activity + Botspice WhatsApp — requires user authorisation before running on UAT.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill all required JBP fields with valid values.
2. Click 'Submit'.
3. Observe the result.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] complete valid JBP on a disposable CP
tcs.expected: A JbpSubmission is created (status ACTIVE, version 1) and the CP is redirected to /jbp/thank-you with the Thank You confirmation (FS 1.6; CP-FRD Module 3).

tcs.scenario: To verify the full submit → Thank You → status-update journey
tcs.description: Verify the end-to-end submission flow: fill, submit, Thank You page, and the Current Cycle status updating to Submitted.
tcs.precond: OPEN cycle; CP not yet submitted. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP. MUTATION: writes a live record — requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the JBP form and fill all fields.
2. Click 'Submit'.
3. Observe the Thank You page.
4. Return to /jbp and read 'Your Status'.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] complete valid JBP on a disposable CP
tcs.expected: Submission succeeds, /jbp/thank-you renders, and on returning to /jbp the 'Your Status' pill reads 'Submitted' and the read-only submission is shown (FS 1.6).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Thank You page renders after submission
tcs.description: Verify that the /jbp/thank-you page is shown immediately after a successful submission.
tcs.precond: A JBP has just been submitted successfully. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP. MUTATION: requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Complete a successful JBP submission.
2. Observe the page.
tcs.expected: The Thank You confirmation page renders at /jbp/thank-you confirming the plan was submitted to the admin team (FS 1.6.2).

tcs.scenario: To verify submission with all checkboxes ticked is accepted
tcs.description: Verify that a valid submission with every Activity/Digital checkbox ticked is accepted.
tcs.precond: OPEN cycle; CP not yet submitted. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP. MUTATION: writes a live record — requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Fill all required fields.
2. Tick all 20 checkboxes.
3. Click 'Submit'.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] all checkboxes ticked on a disposable CP
tcs.expected: The submission is accepted (no upper-bound on checkbox selection) and the Thank You page is shown.

tcs.scenario: To verify one submission per cycle — CTA hidden after submit
tcs.description: Verify that after a successful submission the 'Add New JBP Entry' CTA no longer appears for the cycle.
tcs.precond: The CP has already submitted for the current OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP that has submitted for the open cycle.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /jbp.
2. Open the Current Cycle Entry tab.
tcs.expected: The 'Add New JBP Entry' button is hidden; the submitted plan is shown instead (BRD §4.5, FS 1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify the CTA disappears after a successful submission
tcs.description: Verify that the 'Add New JBP Entry' CTA disappears once the CP has submitted for the cycle.
tcs.precond: The CP has just submitted for the open cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP that has submitted.
tcs.steps:
1. After submitting, return to the Current Cycle Entry tab.
2. Look for the CTA.
tcs.expected: The 'Add New JBP Entry' CTA is no longer shown for this cycle (one submission per cycle, FS 1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify the existing submission renders read-only
tcs.description: Verify that when a submission exists for the current cycle the form fields are shown read-only.
tcs.precond: The CP has a submission for the current OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with a submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /jbp.
2. Open the Current Cycle Entry tab.
tcs.expected: The submitted plan's fields are shown in read-only mode with the version number and status displayed (FS 3.1, 3.2).

tcs.scenario: To verify the submitted JBP is shown read-only on revisit
tcs.description: Verify that revisiting /jbp after submitting shows the plan in read-only format.
tcs.precond: The CP has submitted for the current cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with a submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in and navigate to /jbp.
2. Observe the Current Cycle Entry tab.
tcs.expected: All 14 logical fields display the submitted values in read-only format (FS 3.1).

tcs.scenario: To verify the submission version is displayed
tcs.description: Verify that the read-only view shows the submission version number.
tcs.precond: The CP has a submission. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with a submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the read-only submission view.
2. Read the version indicator.
tcs.expected: The version number is shown (initial submission = version 1) along with the status (FS 3.2).

tcs.scenario: To verify the read-only view shows all 15 activities ticked correctly
tcs.description: Verify that the read-only submission view reflects the exact Activities that were selected.
tcs.precond: A CP has a submission with several activities ticked. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with a known submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the read-only submission view.
2. Compare the ticked activities against what was submitted.
tcs.expected: All activities the CP selected are shown ticked in the read-only view, consistent with the 15-option live set (DOC_DRIFT-003).

tcs.scenario: To verify the read-only view renders digital platform budgets per platform
tcs.description: Verify that the read-only view shows the per-platform digital channel details that were submitted.
tcs.precond: A CP submitted with digital channels selected. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with such a submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the read-only submission view.
2. Inspect the digital channels section.
tcs.expected: The read-only view renders the selected digital platforms (and any per-platform budget) as stored. [VERIFY WITH DEV] per-platform budget capture is implied; confirm the rendered shape.

tcs.scenario: To verify Yes/No read-only values reflect the stored count
tcs.description: Verify that the read-only view shows each Yes/No field's value based on the stored integer/flag.
tcs.precond: A CP submitted with a mix of Yes/No selections. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP with such a submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the read-only submission view.
2. Compare each Yes/No field with what was submitted.
tcs.expected: Each Yes/No field shows the value that was submitted, derived from the stored integer/flag.

tcs.scenario: To verify a second submission for the same cycle is blocked
tcs.description: Verify that attempting to submit a second JBP for the same cycle is prevented.
tcs.precond: The CP has already submitted for the current cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP that has submitted.
tcs.steps: 1. As a CP who has already submitted, attempt to open a new JBP entry / re-submit for the same cycle.
tcs.expected: A second submission is blocked — the entry form/CTA is unavailable and the existing submission is shown (BRD §4.5, FS 1.5 Rule 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify a duplicate submission attempt is blocked (API)
tcs.description: Verify that a duplicate JBP submission for the same cycle is rejected by the backend.
tcs.precond: The CP already has an ACTIVE submission for the cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + a CP with an active submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the JBP submit endpoint a second time for the same CP + cycle.
2. Read the response.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access; CP with active submission
tcs.expected: The backend rejects the duplicate (one active submission per CP per cycle). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact status/message returned for a duplicate.

tcs.scenario: To verify resubmit without an approved edit returns 400 (API)
tcs.description: Verify that resubmitting a JBP without an approved edit request is rejected.
tcs.precond: The CP has an active submission and no approved edit request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the submit/update endpoint without an approved edit request.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend returns 400 — resubmission requires an approved edit request first (FS 2.4).

tcs.scenario: To verify project ownership is NOT enforced (known BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that JBP submission does not enforce project ownership for the CP.
tcs.precond: API access; a CP and a project the CP does not own. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a JBP referencing a project the CP is not associated with.
2. Observe whether it is accepted.
tcs.expected: The submission is accepted even though project ownership is not enforced (KNOWN BUG — see note 13). This documents the gap; recommend enforcing ownership. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the bug still reproduces on current build.

tcs.scenario: To verify the closed-cycle state hides the form
tcs.description: Verify that when the cycle is CLOSED the form is not accessible and the 'Cycle has Closed' message is shown.
tcs.precond: The current cycle is CLOSED. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a CP whose current cycle is closed.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /jbp.
2. Observe the Current Cycle card and tab content.
tcs.expected: The CLOSED badge and a 'Cycle has Closed' message are shown; the form/CTA is not accessible (BRD §4.6; visual-memory screenshot-desktop.png).

tcs.scenario: To verify submissions are not accepted after a cycle closes
tcs.description: Verify that the backend does not accept a JBP submission once the cycle is CLOSED.
tcs.precond: A CLOSED cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access + a CLOSED cycle.
tcs.steps:
1. Attempt to submit a JBP for a CLOSED cycle.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The submission is rejected (cycle not OPEN) (FS 1.5 Rule 1).

tcs.scenario: To verify submit to a CLOSED cycle returns 400 (API)
tcs.description: Verify that posting a submission to a CLOSED cycle returns HTTP 400.
tcs.precond: A CLOSED cycle id. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST the JBP submit endpoint with a CLOSED jbpCycleId.
2. Read the status.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 400 (cycle closed).

tcs.scenario: To verify an edit request is blocked when the cycle is CLOSED
tcs.description: Verify that a CP cannot file an edit request once the cycle is CLOSED.
tcs.precond: The CP has a submission and the cycle is now CLOSED. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] such a CP.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /jbp.
2. Attempt to file an edit request.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CP with submission on a CLOSED cycle
tcs.expected: The edit request is blocked because the cycle is CLOSED (FS 2.2 precondition: cycle still OPEN).

tcs.scenario: To verify an edit request for a CLOSED cycle is rejected (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the edit-request endpoint rejects requests for a CLOSED cycle.
tcs.precond: A submission on a CLOSED cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST an edit request for a submission on a CLOSED cycle.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The edit-request is rejected (cycle closed) (FS 2.2).

tcs.scenario: To verify edit request is available only after submitting (OPEN cycle)
tcs.description: Verify that the edit-request option is available only when the CP has submitted and the cycle is still OPEN.
tcs.precond: The CP has submitted for the current OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] such a CP.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /jbp.
2. Look for the edit-request option in the read-only submission view / Edit Requests tab.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] CP that has submitted on an OPEN cycle
tcs.expected: The edit-request option is available; it would not be available before submitting or when the cycle is CLOSED (FS 2.2).

tcs.scenario: To verify the Request Edit option is visible after submission
tcs.description: Verify that a 'Request Edit' option appears once the CP has a submission for the open cycle.
tcs.precond: The CP has submitted for the current OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] such a CP.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the read-only submission view.
2. Look for the Request Edit control.
tcs.expected: A 'Request Edit' option is visible to the CP (FS 2.1). [VERIFY WITH DEV] the exact label/placement of the Request-Edit control is not transcribed in visual-memory — confirm against the live UI.

tcs.scenario: To verify filing an edit request with reason and revised values
tcs.description: Verify that the CP can submit an edit request describing the changes and the revised values.
tcs.precond: The CP has a submission on an OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP. MUTATION: writes a jbp_edit_requests row — requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Open the Request Edit flow.
2. Enter the changes requested and the revised values.
3. Submit the edit request.
tcs.testData: [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] changes + revised values on a disposable CP
tcs.expected: The edit request is created in the jbp_edit_requests table and appears in the Edit Requests tab pending admin review (FS 2.3).

tcs.scenario: To verify a filed edit request appears in the Edit Requests tab
tcs.description: Verify the end-to-end edit-request flow: file a request and see it listed.
tcs.precond: The CP has a submission on an OPEN cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] disposable CP. MUTATION: writes an edit request — requires user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. File an edit request.
2. Open the Edit Requests tab.
3. Observe the row.
tcs.expected: The newly filed edit request appears as a row in the Edit Requests tab with a pending status.

tcs.scenario: To verify admin approval increments version and expires old
tcs.description: Verify that when the admin approves an edit request the submission updates, the version increments and the old version is marked EXPIRED.
tcs.precond: A pending edit request exists; admin approves it. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin access + a pending edit request. CROSS-PORTAL: approval is done in Admin Portal.
tcs.steps:
1. As admin, approve the CP's edit request (Admin Portal > JBP Management).
2. As CP, refresh /jbp and read the version.
tcs.expected: The submission is updated with the revised values, the version increments (e.g., v1→v2) and the previous version is marked EXPIRED (BRD §4.7, FS 2.4 Rule 2).

tcs.scenario: To verify an approved edit request increments the version to 2
tcs.description: Verify that the CP-side read-only view reflects version 2 after an approved edit request.
tcs.precond: An edit request was approved by admin. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] approved edit request. CROSS-PORTAL.
tcs.steps:
1. After admin approval, navigate to /jbp.
2. Read the version on the read-only view.
tcs.expected: The read-only view shows version 2 with the revised values; version 1 is EXPIRED (FS 2.4).

tcs.scenario: To verify EXPIRED v1 is not shown after v2 becomes active
tcs.description: Verify that once version 2 is active the EXPIRED version 1 is not shown in the CP read-only view.
tcs.precond: An approved edit produced version 2. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] such a submission.
tcs.steps:
1. Navigate to /jbp read-only view.
2. Confirm only the active version is shown.
tcs.expected: Only the active version 2 is shown to the CP; the EXPIRED version 1 is not displayed in the read-only view (FS 2.4).

tcs.scenario: To verify admin rejection preserves the original submission
tcs.description: Verify that when the admin rejects an edit request the original submission is preserved unchanged.
tcs.precond: A pending edit request exists; admin rejects it. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin access. CROSS-PORTAL.
tcs.steps:
1. As admin, reject the edit request with a reason.
2. As CP, view the submission.
tcs.expected: The original submission is preserved unchanged, the version does not increment, and the CP is informed of the rejection reason (FS 2.4 Rule 3/4).

tcs.scenario: To verify a rejected edit request leaves the original intact (no push notification)
tcs.description: Verify that a rejected edit request leaves the submission unchanged and sends no push notification.
tcs.precond: A rejected edit request. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] such a request. CROSS-PORTAL.
tcs.steps: 1. After admin rejection, view the submission and check for push notifications.
tcs.expected: The original submission is intact; no push notification is dispatched on rejection (silent — see note 14; not a bug per silent-UX rule). The CP receives the written reason via the documented channel (FS 2.4 Rule 5). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the rejection-notification channel.

tcs.scenario: To verify a duplicate edit request returns 409 (API)
tcs.description: Verify that filing a second edit request for the same submission while one is pending returns HTTP 409.
tcs.precond: A pending edit request exists. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST a second edit request for the same submission.
2. Read the status.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 409 (a pending edit request already exists).

tcs.scenario: To verify an already-approved-and-editable submission returns 409 on a new request
tcs.description: Verify that a new edit request on an already-approved/editable submission returns 409.
tcs.precond: An approved/editable submission. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST a new edit request against the approved/editable submission.
2. Read the status.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 409 (conflict). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the exact 409 condition vs the duplicate-pending case (CP_JBP_037).

tcs.scenario: To verify submit without prospectId returns 400 (API)
tcs.description: Verify that the JBP submit endpoint rejects a request missing the prospectId.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST the JBP submit endpoint without prospectId.
2. Read the status and body.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 400 (prospectId required).

tcs.scenario: To verify submit with a non-existent jbpCycleId crashes with NPE (known BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that a non-existent jbpCycleId causes a backend null-pointer crash.
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST the submit endpoint with a jbpCycleId that does not exist.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: The backend crashes with an NPE / 500 instead of a clean 400 (KNOWN BUG — note 13). Recommend guarding the missing-cycle case. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the bug still reproduces.

tcs.scenario: To verify an LSQ createActivity failure halts submission before DB write
tcs.description: Verify that if LSQ createActivity fails the JBP submission is halted before the DB write.
tcs.precond: API access; ability to fault LSQ createActivity. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] fault injection. Excludes LSQ creds — observe downstream effect only.
tcs.steps:
1. Force LSQ createActivity to fail.
2. Submit a JBP.
3. Check whether a JbpSubmission row was written.
tcs.expected: Submission is halted before the DB write — no JbpSubmission row is created when createActivity fails. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the ordering on the current build.

tcs.scenario: To verify an LSQ captureLead failure leaves an orphan LSQ activity
tcs.description: Verify the documented behaviour that a captureLead failure after a successful createActivity leaves an orphan LSQ activity.
tcs.precond: API access; ability to fault LSQ captureLead. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] fault injection.
tcs.steps:
1. Allow createActivity to succeed but force captureLead to fail.
2. Submit a JBP.
3. Inspect LSQ + DB state.
tcs.expected: A captureLead failure after a successful createActivity leaves an orphan LSQ activity (no compensating rollback). Document the gap. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm on the current build.

tcs.scenario: To verify the JBP history endpoint returns all versions
tcs.description: Verify that the JBP history endpoint returns every version for the cycle.
tcs.precond: A CP with multiple submission versions. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the JBP history endpoint for the CP/cycle.
2. Inspect the returned versions.
tcs.expected: All versions (including EXPIRED) are returned by the history endpoint for the cycle.

tcs.scenario: To verify the submit endpoint requires authentication
tcs.description: Verify whether the JBP submit endpoint enforces CP authentication.
tcs.precond: API access with NO bearer token. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. Call the JBP submit endpoint with no auth header.
2. Read the status.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] CP-BRD §9 documents that POST /cp/registration is UNAUTHENTICATED — it is NOT stated whether the JBP submit endpoint is also unauthenticated. [To verify] confirm whether /jbp submit requires a valid CP JWT (expected 401 without one) or is open like /cp/registration.

tcs.scenario: To verify injection payloads at the JBP API are handled safely
tcs.description: Verify that SQLi/XSS payloads sent to JBP API fields are handled safely (no SQL error, no script reflection).
tcs.precond: API access. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST the submit/edit endpoint with an injection payload in a text field.
2. Read the response.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] the backend should reject/sanitise safely with no SQL error and no reflected script. [To verify] confirm backend sanitisation for JBP endpoints.

tcs.scenario: To verify an expired edit window returns 403 (API)
tcs.description: Verify that filing an edit request after the edit window has expired returns HTTP 403.
tcs.precond: A submission whose edit window has expired. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access.
tcs.steps:
1. POST an edit request after the edit window has expired.
2. Read the status.
tcs.expected: The endpoint returns HTTP 403 (edit window expired).

tcs.scenario: To verify the isJbpSubmitted login flag counts EXPIRED rows (known BUG)
tcs.description: Verify the documented bug that the login-time isJbpSubmitted flag includes EXPIRED submission rows.
tcs.precond: A CP with only EXPIRED submission rows for the cycle. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] such a CP.
tcs.steps:
1. Log in as a CP whose only rows for the cycle are EXPIRED.
2. Inspect the isJbpSubmitted flag / resulting UI state.
tcs.expected: isJbpSubmitted is computed as true even though only EXPIRED rows exist (KNOWN BUG — note 13). Recommend excluding EXPIRED rows. [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the bug reproduces on the current build.

tcs.scenario: To verify a non-CP role cannot access /jbp
tcs.description: Verify that a user without the CP role (role ID 3) cannot access the CP JBP screen.
tcs.precond: A session for a non-CP role (e.g., Admin/SM). [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] a non-CP session.
tcs.steps:
1. With a non-CP session, navigate to https://uat-web.xrportal.in/jbp.
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] CP-FRD §7 requires role ID 3; cross-role access behaviour on /jbp is not documented. [To verify] confirm a non-CP role is blocked/redirected and cannot view JBP data (multi-tenant isolation).

tcs.scenario: To verify CP-to-CP data isolation on JBP submissions
tcs.description: Verify that a CP cannot view or act on another CP's JBP submission.
tcs.precond: Two CPs with their own submissions. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] API access for two CPs.
tcs.steps:
1. As CP-A, attempt to read CP-B's JBP submission/history (by id).
2. Observe the result.
tcs.expected: [VERIFY WITH DEV] CP isolation is documented for customer records (BRD §4.1, brokerId match) but not explicitly for JBP submissions. [To verify] confirm CP-A cannot access CP-B's JBP submission (expected 403/empty).

tcs.scenario: To verify auth requests use HTTPS with no sensitive data in the URL
tcs.description: Verify that the JBP screen and its API calls are HTTPS and do not carry sensitive data in the URL.
tcs.precond: DevTools open on /jbp.
tcs.steps:
1. Confirm the address bar shows https:// on /jbp.
2. Capture the JBP submit/history requests in the Network tab.
3. Check the method and URL.
tcs.expected: All JBP requests are HTTPS; submission payloads are sent in the request body (POST), not in the URL/query; no mixed-content warnings.

tcs.scenario: To verify a submitted JBP appears in Admin > JBP Management > Submissions
tcs.description: Verify the cross-module flow: a CP submission becomes visible to the admin for review.
tcs.precond: A CP has submitted a JBP. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] admin access. CROSS-PORTAL.
tcs.steps:
1. As CP, submit a JBP.
2. As admin, open Admin Portal > JBP Management > Submissions tab.
3. Locate the submission.
tcs.expected: The CP's submission appears in the Admin Portal JBP Management Submissions tab for review (FS 1.6.3).

tcs.scenario: To verify submission triggers the Botspice WhatsApp template
tcs.description: Verify that a successful JBP submission dispatches the Botspice WhatsApp template 'jbplaunchtwo_new' (15 vars), NOT Kaleyra.
tcs.precond: A successful JBP submission. [TEST_DATA_REQUIRED] outbound message-log access. MUTATION: requires a real submission — user authorisation.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit a JBP.
2. Inspect the outbound notification logs.
tcs.expected: A Botspice WhatsApp message using template 'jbplaunchtwo_new' (15 variables) is dispatched on submission; no Kaleyra OTP/notification is involved (note 14). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm the 15 variables on the current build.

tcs.scenario: To verify no notification is sent on a blocked/validation-failed submit
tcs.description: Verify that a submission blocked by validation sends NO WhatsApp/SMS/email (silent — no side-effect on failure).
tcs.precond: The JBP form is open and will fail validation.
tcs.steps:
1. Submit an invalid/empty form (blocked at validation).
2. Check outbound message logs.
tcs.expected: No Botspice WhatsApp / SMS / email is dispatched because no JbpSubmission was created; absence of a notification here is correct (silent-by-design, note 8). [VERIFY WITH DEV] confirm no side-channel fires on a blocked submit.
